title: A Conceptual Framework for Promoting Neighborhood Social Sustainability: A Review of Literature
abstract: Social sustainability is a component of sustainability that has received attention in recent years. Its objective is to promote social well-being and improve the quality of life of people. Built environments play a significant role in social well-being in cities. Neighborhoods, therefore, being the essential physical and social components of cities, offer great opportunities for investigating the social sustainability of built environments. This paper examines social sustainability to produce a theoretical framework to examine the social issues related to cities. It employs a document survey as a research method and examines published literature systematically, to shed light on the multifaceted discourse surrounding social sustainability. It elucidates its diverse manifestations portrayed within scholarly discourse. The findings show that the concept revolves around two concepts: physical and non-physical attributes. They consist of several indicators measurable on objective and subjective criteria. These relate to both physical and non-physical attributes, as well as the aspirations and experiences of people, as a component of social sustainability. This research offers valuable insights into neighborhood-related social sustainability, establishing a foundation for academic investigations. It presents a novel framework of the two pillars of social sustainability, to clarify its multifaceted nature. The framework can help in developing a tool for a holistic comprehension of social sustainability

title: Treatment of anterior cruciate ligament injuries in older adults: A clinical review
abstract: The anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) is essential for knee joint stability. Although ACL injuries primarily affect young and middle-aged athletes, their incidence among older adults is increasing. Substantial or complete ACL rupture may cause persistent instability despite conservative treatment; in such cases, ACL reconstruction (ACLR) surgery is generally considered the standard surgical treatment. Because older adults often have osteoporosis, joint degeneration, and comorbidities, as well as lower functional demands than younger patients, some surgeons recommend conservative treatment. However, recent studies have found that patients who undergo ACLR and ACL repair have better postoperative functional recovery than those who receive conservative treatment, although there remains no clear consensus regarding the optimal treatment. This review examines the characteristics of ACL injuries in older adults and compares treatment methods, with the aim of improving the management of these patients. Current evidence indicates that older adults who undergo ACLR achieve comparable functional outcomes to younger patients, suggesting that treatment decisions should focus on functional needs and overall health rather than age or comorbidities alone. All-inside techniques may provide better outcomes in older adults, while supplementary reinforcement fixation may benefit patients with osteoporosis.

title: Traditional Sports Games for Character Development in Preservice Primary Teachers
abstract: Traditional sports and games are widely discussed as culturally grounded resources for character education, yet research predominantly concerns children and provides limited guidance on translating gameplay into assessable professional learning for preservice primary teachers. This article synthesizes recent evidence on the potential of traditional games to support character development and proposes an instructional and assessment framework for Primary School Teacher Education (PGSD) students. A critical narrative review examined 25 journal articles published between 2023 and 2026, purposively selected for their relevance to traditional games, physical education, social and moral learning, and preservice teacher preparation. Thematic synthesis identified three interconnected learning mechanisms: rule-governed cooperation and fair competition, emotionally meaningful interaction followed by guided reflection, and pedagogical transfer to primary school lesson design. These themes informed a five-stage framework comprising value orientation, inclusive gameplay, behavioral observation, reflective dialogue, and assessment linked to teaching transfer. Supporting resources include illustrative mappings between games and behavioral indicators, a six-session learning plan, and an analytic observation rubric. The synthesis suggests that traditional games provide plausible opportunities to practice cooperation, discipline, honesty, responsibility, sportsmanship, tolerance, and leadership. However, the review does not establish their causal effectiveness for PGSD students. The proposed framework offers a context-sensitive basis for connecting culturally grounded character education with professional learning in preservice teacher preparation. Pilot implementation involving repeated behavioral assessment and comparisons across learning contexts is needed to evaluate its applicability and effectiveness.

title: The Influence Of Influencer Credibility and Expertise On Repurchase Intention Of Hmns Perfume: The Mediating Role Of Consumer Trust
journal: International Journal of Management and Business Economics
abstract: This study investigates how influencer credibility and expertise shape repurchase intention among consumers of HMNS perfume, with consumer trust positioned as a mediating variable. The fragrance sector has grown rapidly, and digital influencers now play a central role in how consumers form opinions and make choices about scent products. Data were gathered through an online survey involving 144 respondents who had purchased HMNS perfume and had encountered influencer content on social media. The analysis relied on SEM-PLS with SmartPLS 4. The results show that influencer credibility (β = 0.354, t = 5.346, p < 0.001) and expertise (β = 0.465, t = 7.417, p < 0.001) both have positive and significant effects on consumer trust. Consumer trust, in turn, significantly influences repurchase intention (β = 0.508, t = 8.906, p < 0.001). In addition, consumer trust significantly mediates the relationship between credibility (β = 0.180, t = 4.311, p < 0.001) and expertise (β = 0.236, t = 5.733, p < 0.001) on repurchase intention. The model explains 36.7% of the variance in consumer trust and 25.8% of the variance in repurchase intention. These findings suggest that HMNS should work with influencers who are not only well-known but also genuinely credible and knowledgeable about fragrance. Trust turns out to be the key pathway through which influencer qualities lead to repeat purchase intention. This study adds to the influencer marketing literature by showing how trust mediates these relationships for experience-based products like perfume.

title: Investigating the Impact of AI-Facilitated Socratic Dialogue on Critical Thinking Skills
journal: International Journal of Teacher Education Research Studies (IJTERS)
abstract: This mixed-method study aims to explore the impact of having Socratic dialogue with artificial intelligence (AI) on students' critical thinking skills’ performance. The data were gathered from 35 foundation-level students. The study utilised a Watson Glaser critical thinking pre-test and post-test to measure their critical thinking abilities and a questionnaire to gather their perception of AI usage. During the intervention, students were engaged in structured AI-facilitated Socratic questioning sessions weekly. Data were analysed using paired-sample t-tests and linear regression, while survey responses were examined for thematic trends. Even though the data collected shows that students have a positive perception of using AI, there is no statistically significant difference between the pre- and post-tests (p > .05). The finding shows that students’ critical thinking performance did not improve throughout the study. Furthermore, the results for the linear regression (R² = 0.038, p > .05) show that there is very little correlation between students’ perception and their critical thinking performance. The study reveals the gap between students’ positive perception of using AI and their critical thinking skill development.

title: ‘AFTER THE CARAVELS SAILED’: CONTINUING WRONG, STATE RESPONSIBILITY, AND THE UNITED NATIONS RESOLUTION ON THE SLAVE TRADE
journal: Journal of Advance Research in Social Science and Humanities (ISSN 2208-2387)
abstract: This article examines whether the United Nations General Assembly’s Resolution 80/250, which declares the transatlantic trafficking of enslaved Africans and the racialised chattel enslavement of Africans the ‘gravest crime against humanity’ and identifies claims for reparations as ‘a concrete step towards remedying historical wrongs’, can be grounded in the law of state responsibility. The states that opposed the Resolution, and most of those that abstained, did not dispute the gravity of the trade. Rather, they denied that it could ground a present legal remedy, invoking the intertemporal principle of the Island of Palmas award. This article argues that this objection does not withstand scrutiny. It rests on a partial reading of Island of Palmas, which distinguishes the creation of a legal situation from its continued existence; it assumes a uniform lawfulness which the nineteenth-century treaty record contradicts; and it overlooks the distinction between Article 13 and Articles 14(2) and 15 of the Articles on State Responsibility. The article then develops a ‘doctrine of living harm’, according to which a situation originating in the trade is a continuing wrong only where a determinate obligation binds the state now, the state presently controls the situation, and its present conduct fails to conform to that obligation. Drawing on the case law of the Inter-American Court of Human Rights, the European Court of Human Rights, and the International Court of Justice, the article identifies three modes of continuing wrong (persisting illicit possession, composite wrong, and inherited structural injury) and the five obligations that follow from them.

title: Yandangshan Dendrobium officinale flower flavonoids alleviate dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis in association with local intestinal ecological remodeling
abstract: Abstract Objectives Ulcerative colitis arises from epithelial barrier disruption, gut microbial dysbiosis, and aberrant mucosal immune activation. Given that many food-derived flavonoids achieve limited systemic exposure after oral administration, how local intestinal activity translates into host tissue protection remains a central question. Resolving this process is challenging because microbial communities, metabolite outputs, and mucosal responses operate across distinct biological levels and often yield disconnected evidence. Materials and Methods : Here, we studied chemically consistent Dendrobium officinale flower flavonoids (DOFF), validated across six independent batches by liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS), and integrated absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) prediction, conventional and antibiotic-perturbed dextran sulfate sodium (DSS) colitis models, 16S rRNA sequencing, targeted short-chain fatty acid quantification, untargeted fecal metabolomics, host-response network analysis, single-cell virtual knockout, and whole-slide artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted spatial pathology. Results DOFF reduced dextran sulfate sodium-induced disease activity and colonic injury, restored ZO-1- and Occludin-associated barrier integrity, reconfigured gut microbial structure and fecal metabolic profiles, and suppressed TLR4/MYD88/NF-κB signaling; computational integration and single-cell virtual knockout further prioritized FFAR2/HCAR2, TLR4/RELA, and EGFR/LGR5 as candidate host targets associated with metabolite sensing, inflammatory regulation, and epithelial repair, respectively, while DOFF retained partial tissue protection after broad-spectrum antibiotic perturbation, accompanied by limited shifts in residual microbiota and AI-predicted spatial pathology features. Conclusions These findings support a local ecology-first working model in which DOFF-associated microbiota-metabolite remodeling coincides with epithelial barrier restoration and mucosal inflammatory suppression without necessarily requiring high systemic exposure or action through a single host target, although direct causal roles for the microbiota, key metabolites, and host receptors require further validation.

title: The Dynamics of Crime and the Contemporary World: Moral and Existentialist Dilemmas in Adaobi Nwaubani’s I Do Not Come to you by Chance
journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SOCIAL SCIENCE HUMANITY & MANAGEMENT RESEARCH
abstract: Literature reflects the milieu and the moment, and echoes society’s zeitgeist and the enabling contexts. It recreates society vividly with a view to projecting its positives sides and values and attacking its imperfections. Literature offers qualitative evaluation of contemporary trends in the society in a bid to retain the cherished and discard the obnoxious. These assertions constitute the thrust of this study which examines the depiction of crime and related trends in the contemporary Nigerian society as inscribed in Adaobi Nwaubani’s I Do Not Come to You by Chance. Specifically, the work interrogates the moral, economic, social, and existential circumstances that make criminal behaviours appear attractive or even necessary to an individual. The study, which adopts Existentialism as its theoretical framework, argues that contemporary crime has moved beyond judging the criminal to interrogating the conditions that produce, normalise, justify, or complicate criminal behaviour. The research finds unmitigated criminalities typified by advanced fee fraud, cybercrime, unbridled corruption, and decay/erosion of society’s fundamental values as some of the amoral, cynical, and gloomy issues raised in Nwaubani’s realistic artistry. The study submits that beyond being a mere willful act, behaviour or habit, crime, as depicted in Ubani’s craft, is a consequence of social and economic pressure which is given impetus by the amazingly weak, vacillating, complacent, and inept political leadership as well as insidiously weakening societal values. Nwaubani’s work aptly recreates existentialist and modernist dystopia in contemporary times characterised by pessimism, hedonism, anxiety, agony, nihilism, criminalities, despair, and death.
